# Configure Auth0 for agent IAM

@include 'alerts/enterprise-and-hcp.mdx'

Configure users, applications, and Actions in Auth0 so Auth0 can issue
on-behalf-of (OBO) access tokens with Rich Authorization Request (RAR) claims
for Vault Enterprise agentic IAM. Auth0 issues the delegated token through
[Custom Token Exchange](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/custom-token-exchange/configure-custom-token-exchange)
(RFC 8693).


## Before you start

- **You must have an Auth0 tenant with
  an [Auth0 Enterprise](https://auth0.com/pricing) license**. Custom Token
  Exchange requires a paid Enterprise license. Ask your Auth0 Enterprise
  administrator for access to an Enterprise tenant, and note the tenant name and
  region. The tenant name appears in the top left of the Auth0 dashboard and on
  the **Settings** > **General** page.

- **You must have sufficient permission for your Auth0 tenant**. You must have
  permission to create applications, APIs, users, and Actions, and to use the
  Auth0 Management API.

- **You must run Vault 2.2.0 or later**. Auth0 reserves the
  `authorization_details` claim, so the RAR arrives in a custom claim. Vault
  2.2.0 adds the `authorization_details_claim` profile parameter to read it.

- **You must have the [`oauth2c`](https://github.com/SecureAuthCorp/oauth2c) CLI**
  installed and in your system `PATH` to interact with OAuth 2.0 authorization
  servers.

- **You must have `curl` and `jq`** installed to call the Auth0 Management API.

<Highlight title="Try the tutorial">

To walk through an robust, end-to-end agentic IAM workflow using Docker
containers, we also offer an in-depth tutorial on
[Securing agent permissions with Vault](/vault/tutorials/enterprise/secure-agent-permissions-with-vault).

</Highlight>


## Step 1: Create a custom API

The API represents the audience that validates the JWT Auth0 issues.

1. Save your Auth0 tenant domain as an environment variable:

    ```shell-session
    $ export APP_DOMAIN="<your_tenant>.us.auth0.com"
    ```

1. Navigate to **Applications** > **APIs**.

1. Click **Create API**.

1. In the **Name** field, enter a name value (for example, `vault-api`).

1. In the **Identifier** field, provide the API address of you Vault cluster.
   The identifier value eventually becomes the JWT `aud` claim.

1. For **JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile**, select **RFC 9068**.

1. Scroll down and click **Create**.

1. Click the **Settings**.

1. Scroll down to **RBAC Settings**.

1. Click the toggle to switch on **Enable RBAC**.

1. Click the toggle to switch on **Add Permissions in the Access Token**.

1. Click **Save**.

1. Save the API identifier as `AUDIENCE_ADDR` so you can request the correct
   audience in access tokens:

    ```shell-session
    $ export AUDIENCE_ADDR=${VAULT_ADDR}/v1
    ```


## Step 2: Create a user

Create a user to represent the human subject who delegates authority to the
agent.

1. Navigate to **User Management** > **Users**.

1. Click **Create User**.

1. Select **Create via UI**.

1. Enter an **Email** and a **Password** with at least one number and one
   special character.

1. Click **Create**.

1. On the user page, click **Edit** next to **Email**, and mark the email as
   verified.

1. Copy the **user_id** value from the user page and save it as an environment
   variable. The value contains a pipe character, so wrap the string in single
   quotes:

    ```shell-session
    $ export SUBJECT_ID='auth0|<user_id>'
    ```


## Step 3: Create an agent application

The agent authenticates to Auth0 as a machine-to-machine application.

1. Navigate to **Applications** > **Applications**, then click
   **Create Application**.

1. In the **Name** field, enter a name for the agent (for example, `ai-agent`).

1. Select **Machine to Machine Applications**.

1. Click **Create**.

1. Select the API you created and click **Authorize**.

1. Open the **Settings** page and save the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
   as environment variables:

    ```shell-session
    $ export                                     \
        AGENT_ID="<agent_client_id>"             \
        AGENT_SECRET="<agent_client_secret>"
    ```

1. Click **Advanced Settings**.

1. Open the **Grant Types** tab and check only **Client Credentials**.

1. Click **Save**.


## Step 4: Create an Auth0 application

The application requests tokens for the user and performs the token exchange.

1. Navigate to **Applications** > **Applications**, then click
   **Create Application**.

1. Enter a custom name for the **Name** field.

1. Select **Regular Web Application**.

1. Click **Create**.

1. Open the **Settings** page and note the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**
   for your application.

1. Scroll to **Application URIs** section.

1. Add the default callback for `oauth2c` to the **Allowed Callback URLs** list,
   `http://localhost:9876/callback`, so you can request user tokens later.

1. Click **Advanced Settings**.

1. Click **OAuth**.

1. In the **Allowed APPs/APIs** field, enter your Vault API address (for example,
   `https://<vault-addr>:8200/v1`).

1. Open the **Grant Types** tab and check **Authorization Code**.

1. Open the **Endpoints** tab and record both the **OAuth Authorization URL**
   and the **JSON Web Key Set URL** values for use later.

1. Click **Save**.

1. Save the application values as environment variables:

    ```shell-session
    $ export                                                      \
        APP_AUTH_URL="https://${APP_DOMAIN}/authorize"            \
        APP_ID="<application_client_id>"                         \
        SECRET_VALUE="<application_client_secret>"               \
        JWKS_URI="https://${APP_DOMAIN}/.well-known/jwks.json"    \
        ISSUER="https://${APP_DOMAIN}/"
    ```


## Step 5: Grant application access

With the API and both applications created, grant client access from the API
to each application.

1. Navigate to **Auth0 Dashboard** > **Applications** > **APIs**.

1. Select the API you created.

1. Click **Application Access**.

1. Find your application, and click **Edit**.

1. Click **Grant Access**.

1. Click the **Always grant all permissions** checkbox.

1. Click **Save**.

1. Repeat the process for the agent application.


## Step 6: Get a Management API access token

You need a Management API access token to enable Custom Token Exchange and
create a token exchange profile. The Auth0 dashboard does not expose these
settings.

1. Navigate to **Applications** > **APIs**.

1. Click **Auth0 Management API**.

1. Click the **Advanced** tab.

   {/* TODO: Confirm whether Create & Authorize Test Application is on the Advanced tab or the API Explorer tab. */}

1. Click **Create & Authorize Test Application**.

1. Open the **API Explorer** tab, copy the token, and save it as an environment
   variable:

    ```shell-session
    $ export MGMT_TOKEN="<management_api_token>"
    ```

The token is valid for one day (86400 seconds). Generate a new token from the
**API Explorer** tab if you continue beyond a day.


## Step 7: Enable Custom Token Exchange

Use the Management API to allow your application to use custom token exchange
profiles:

```shell-session
$ curl --request PATCH                                          \
    --url "https://${APP_DOMAIN}/api/v2/clients/${APP_ID}"      \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${MGMT_TOKEN}"              \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json'                   \
    --data '{"token_exchange": {"allow_any_profile_of_type": ["custom_authentication"]}}'
```

Confirm that `is_first_party` and `oidc_conformant` are both `true` in the
response. Token exchange fails if either value is `false`.


## Step 8: Create a Custom Token Exchange Action

The Custom Token Exchange Action verifies the subject (human) and actor (agent)
tokens, sets the token subject, adds the RFC 8693 `act` claim, and passes any
requested `authorization_details` to the Post Login Action. Review the Auth0
coding guidelines for Actions before you adapt the code.

1. Navigate to **Actions** > **Library**.

1. Click **Create Action** and select **Create Custom Action**.

1. In the **Name** field, enter `process_obo_rar_token_cte`.

1. For **Trigger**, select **Custom Token Exchange**.

1. For **Runtime**, keep **Node 22**.

1. Click **Create**.

   {/* TODO: Confirm whether the jose module must be added under the Action's Dependencies before deploying. */}

1. Replace the editor contents with the following code. Replace
   `<your_tenant>.us.auth0.com` with your `APP_DOMAIN` value and
   `<application_client_id>` with your `APP_ID` value:

    ```javascript
    const { createRemoteJWKSet, jwtVerify } = require('jose');

    const AUTH0_DOMAIN = '<your_tenant>.us.auth0.com';
    const EXPECTED_ISSUER = `https://${AUTH0_DOMAIN}/`;
    const JWKS = createRemoteJWKSet(new URL(`https://${AUTH0_DOMAIN}/.well-known/jwks.json`));

    // Applications allowed to perform the token exchange
    const ALLOWED_CLIENT_IDS = new Set(['<application_client_id>']);

    async function verifyTenantJwt(token) {
      const { payload } = await jwtVerify(token, JWKS, {
        issuer: EXPECTED_ISSUER,
        algorithms: ['RS256'],
        clockTolerance: '10s'
      });
      return payload;
    }

    exports.onExecuteCustomTokenExchange = async (event, api) => {
      if (!ALLOWED_CLIENT_IDS.has(event.client.client_id)) {
        return api.access.deny('invalid_client', 'Client is not authorized for token exchange.');
      }

      const subjectToken = event.transaction?.subject_token;
      const actorToken = event.transaction?.actor_token || event.request.body?.actor_token;

      if (!subjectToken) {
        return api.access.rejectInvalidSubjectToken('Missing required subject_token.');
      }

      // Verify the subject token and set the subject user
      let subjectPayload;
      try {
        subjectPayload = await verifyTenantJwt(subjectToken);
      } catch (err) {
        return api.access.rejectInvalidSubjectToken(`Subject token verification failed: ${err.message}`);
      }
      if (!subjectPayload.sub) {
        return api.access.rejectInvalidSubjectToken('Subject token does not contain a "sub" claim.');
      }
      api.authentication.setUserById(subjectPayload.sub);

      // Verify the actor token and add the act claim
      if (actorToken) {
        let actorPayload;
        try {
          actorPayload = await verifyTenantJwt(actorToken);
        } catch (err) {
          return api.access.deny('invalid_request', `Actor token verification failed: ${err.message}`);
        }
        if (actorPayload.sub) {
          api.authentication.setActor({ sub: actorPayload.sub });
        }
      }

      // Pass the requested RAR to the Post Login Action
      const rawRar = event.request.body?.authorization_details;
      if (rawRar) {
        let parsedRar = rawRar;
        if (typeof rawRar === 'string') {
          try {
            parsedRar = JSON.parse(rawRar);
          } catch {
            return api.access.deny('invalid_request', 'Invalid JSON in authorization_details.');
          }
        }
        api.user.setAppMetadata('transient_rar_details', parsedRar);
      }
    };
    ```

1. Click **Deploy**.

1. Copy the Action ID from the end of the browser address bar
   (`.../actions/library/details/<action_id>`) and save it as an environment
   variable:

    ```shell-session
    $ export CTE_ACTION_ID="<action_id>"
    ```


## Step 9: Create a token exchange profile

A token exchange profile links a custom subject token type to the Action that
handles it. Use the Management API to link the
`urn:vault:params:oauth:token-type:access_token` subject token type to the
Custom Token Exchange Action:

```shell-session
$ curl --request POST                                                 \
    --url "https://${APP_DOMAIN}/api/v2/token-exchange-profiles"      \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${MGMT_TOKEN}"                    \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/json'                         \
    --data '{
      "name": "vault-obo-rar",
      "subject_token_type": "urn:vault:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
      "action_id": "'"${CTE_ACTION_ID}"'",
      "type": "custom_authentication"
    }'
```

Refer to the Auth0
[custom token exchange profile](https://auth0.com/docs/authenticate/custom-token-exchange/configure-custom-token-exchange#create-custom-token-exchange-profile)
documentation for more information.


## Step 10: Create a Post Login Action

The Post Login Action copies the requested RAR into the access token. Auth0
reserves the `authorization_details` claim, so the Action writes the RAR to a
namespaced custom claim, such as
`https://vault.example.com/authorization_details`.

1. Navigate to **Actions** > **Library**.

1. Click **Create Action** and select **Create Custom Action**.

1. In the **Name** field, enter `inject_rar_claims_post_login`.

1. For **Trigger**, select **Login / Post Login**.

1. For **Runtime**, keep **Node 22**.

1. Click **Create**.

1. Replace the editor contents with the following code:

    ```javascript
    exports.onExecutePostLogin = async (event, api) => {
      const rarDetails = event.user.app_metadata?.transient_rar_details;
      const rarClaimNamespace = 'https://vault.example.com';

      if (rarDetails) {
        api.accessToken.setCustomClaim(`${rarClaimNamespace}/authorization_details`, rarDetails);
        api.user.setAppMetadata('transient_rar_details', null);
      }
    };
    ```

1. Click **Deploy**.

1. Navigate to **Actions** > **Triggers** and click **post-login**.

1. Drag `inject_rar_claims_post_login` from the **Add Action** pane to a
   position between **Start** and **Complete**.

1. Click **Apply**.

1. Save the custom claim name as an environment variable. Set the
   `authorization_details_claim` parameter of your OAuth resource server profile
   to this value:

    ```shell-session
    $ export RAR_CLAIM="https://vault.example.com/authorization_details"
    ```


## Step 11: Save your provider information

Confirm your subject and actor details from Auth0. To configure agentic IAM,
you must have the following information:

Value                | Environmental variable | Description
-------------------- | ---------------------- | -----------
Authorization URL    | `APP_AUTH_URL`         | Authorization URL of the application
Domain address       | `APP_DOMAIN`           | Domain of your Auth0 tenant
Auth0 client ID      | `APP_ID`               | Client ID of the application you registered in Auth0
Client secret value  | `SECRET_VALUE`         | Client secret associated with your application
Agent client ID      | `AGENT_ID`             | Client ID of the agent application
Agent client secret  | `AGENT_SECRET`         | Client secret associated with the agent application
Issuer URL           | `ISSUER`               | `iss` URL for your tenant
Subject ID           | `SUBJECT_ID`           | `sub` claim for the human user (the Auth0 user ID)
Agent subject ID     | `EXTERNAL_ID`          | `sub` claim for the agent, the agent client ID followed by `@clients`
Key endpoint         | `JWKS_URI`             | URL where clients can download public keys (JWKS) from your tenant
Audience address     | `AUDIENCE_ADDR`        | Vault cluster address including the API version, `/v1`
RAR claim name       | `RAR_CLAIM`            | Custom claim that carries the RAR

Save the agent subject ID:

```shell-session
$ export EXTERNAL_ID="${AGENT_ID}@clients"
```

If you have not already, we recommend setting the following environment
variables to make Vault configuration more convenient:

```shell-session
$ export                                \
   VAULT_ADDR="<your_vault_server_url>" \
   APP_AUTH_URL="<app_auth_url>"        \
   APP_DOMAIN="<app_domain>"            \
   APP_ID="<app_client_id>"             \
   SECRET_VALUE="<app_client_secret>"   \
   AGENT_ID="<agent_client_id>"         \
   AGENT_SECRET="<agent_client_secret>" \
   ISSUER="<app_iss_url>"               \
   SUBJECT_ID="<subject_user_id>"       \
   EXTERNAL_ID="<agent_client_id>@clients" \
   JWKS_URI="<app_jwks_url>"            \
   AUDIENCE_ADDR="<aud_address>"        \
   RAR_CLAIM="<rar_claim_name>"
```

To debug a failed token issuance or exchange, navigate to **Monitoring** >
**Logs** in the Auth0 dashboard. Output from `console.log` statements in an
Action appears in the Action logs.
